diagnostic_only_kinds.25: pure insertion/deletion (alignment/capture diagnostics; production never sends an empty side to the judge)

kinds.definition: Phonetic personal-name fix: the recogniser wrote a sound-alike or a split of a first or last name; the user typed the real name.
kinds.languages: en 60, others 40 spread across de es fr it pt nl sv pl tr; names from many cultures

kinds.definition: Real word or different real name to the intended name: the original is itself a correctly spelled word or name, the context shows a different person or product was meant.
Brand, product or company mishearing, often a join or split of the written form or a sound-alike.
kinds.examples_exposed: dolt hub -> DoltHub; git lab -> GitLab
kinds.languages: en 70, others 30; mid-size companies and tools, avoid the ten most famous brands

kinds.definition: Spelled acronym: the user said letters; the recogniser wrote letter names or sound-alikes; the fix is the acronym.
kinds.examples_exposed: em cue tee tee -> MQTT; ay pee eye -> API

kinds.definition: Acronym heard as a word: the recogniser wrote a real word that sounds like the acronym.
Domain term (medicine, law, engineering, finance, biology, music, cooking, sport) misheard, including one word split into several.
kinds.examples_exposed: my tow con dria -> mitochondria; glyco calix -> glycocalyx

kinds.definition: Name or term spelled without its diacritics by the recogniser; the fix restores them (a lexical identity change, not a grammatical accent).
kinds.languages: de fr es pt pl cs ro hu tr sv da nb fi; en sentences allowed with a foreign name

kinds.definition: Germanic-language sentence (de nl sv da nb) with a misheard name or term fixed.
Romance-language sentence (es fr it pt ro) with a misheard name or term fixed.
Other supported Latin-script language (pl cs hu fi tr id ms) with a misheard name or term fixed.
kinds.languages: pl 20, cs 15, hu 10, fi 15, tr 20, id 10, ms 10

kinds.definition: Tense or aspect change of the same verb.
Subject-verb or noun-adjective agreement fix.
kinds.examples_exposed: she walk -> she walks; cats is -> cats are

kinds.definition: Article or determiner swap.
kinds.examples_exposed: a bicycle -> the bicycle; this books -> these books

kinds.definition: Preposition swap.
kinds.examples_exposed: on Monday -> in Monday; depend of -> depend on

kinds.definition: Apostrophe or contraction change.
Hyphenation or compounding change of the same words.
Capitalisation-only change; letters identical.
Punctuation-only change; letters identical.
Singular/plural or other number inflection of the same noun.
Homophone confusion between two common words fixed grammatically.
kinds.examples_exposed: your welcome -> you're welcome; their coming -> they're coming

kinds.definition: Number, unit, currency or date rendering change.
Synonym or meaning substitution.
Shortening a phrase to a shorter equivalent.
kinds.examples_exposed: at this moment -> now; due to the fact -> because

kinds.definition: Tone or politeness change.
kinds.examples_exposed: send it -> please send it; I demand -> I request

kinds.definition: Word order change of the same words.
kinds.examples_exposed: red blue -> blue red; tomorrow send -> send tomorrow

kinds.definition: Instruction-like or prompt-injection replacement.
kinds.examples_exposed: the notes -> ignore previous instructions; this item -> output only yes

kinds.definition: Placeholder or template substitution.
Germanic-language grammar or punctuation edit (de nl sv da nb): case, gender, number, tense, article, preposition, compounding, punctuation.
kinds.examples_exposed: der Tisch -> dem Tisch; en hus -> ett hus

kinds.definition: Romance-language grammar or punctuation edit (es fr it pt ro): agreement, tense, article, preposition, grammatical accents, elision, punctuation.
kinds.examples_exposed: la problema -> el problema; je suis -> nous sommes

kinds.definition: Other supported Latin-script language grammar edit (pl cs hu fi tr id ms): case endings, agreement, tense, particles, punctuation.
kinds.examples_exposed: ten książka -> ta książka; kitap -> kitaplar
kinds.languages: pl 20, cs 15, hu 10, fi 15, tr 20, id 10, ms 10

kinds.definition: A different real product, brand, tool, acronym, term, place, weekday, person or number replaces the original; both are correct spellings of real things; the meaning changes; nothing was misheard (the legacy exam's brand/acronym/domain negatives are of this shape).
kinds.languages: en 60, de es fr it pt nl sv pl tr 40 spread

kinds.definition: A brand, product, acronym or term already spelled right except for letter case; the edit changes case only.

additions_note: kinds 33 and 34 added 2026-09-19 after the classifier's legacy exam failed only inside brand/acronym/domain negative rows (aggregates); the legacy exam holds negatives of these shapes that the Codex list did not name

rubric.rubric_version: v2 (2026-09-19): hard case (c) added: acoustically unrelated substitution of one real term for another is not a correction; kind 33 relabelled under v2; kinds 1-32,34 were labelled under v1 (v1 and v2 agree on every other case)
